It is said that those with horns, spread teeth, or extended claws, whether they fly above or crawl below, are called birds and beasts. They do not necessarily lack the hearts of humans. Although they have human hearts, because of their physical forms they are treated with distance. <note>The author argues that external appearance does not dictate internal nature.</note>

The clan leaders Paoxi <note>also known as Fuxi, the first of the Three Sovereigns</note>, Nuwa, Shennong, and the Great Xia ruler <note>Yu the Great</note> had the bodies of snakes with human faces, or the heads of oxen with the noses of tigers. These had the physical forms of non-humans, yet they possessed the virtues of Great Sages. In contrast, Jie of Xia, Zhou of Yin, Huan of Lu, and Mu of Chu all had appearances and sensory organs <note>the seven apertures of the head: eyes, ears, nostrils, and mouth</note> identical to other humans, yet they possessed the hearts of birds and beasts. If the masses persist in looking only at physical form to find supreme wisdom, they will never come close to achieving it.

<margin>These two points are acceptable.</margin>
<margin>Liezi, Yellow Emperor chapter.</margin>

The <term>Huangdi</term> <gloss>Yellow Emperor</gloss> fought against the <term>Yandi</term> <gloss>Flame Emperor</gloss> at the wilderness of <term>Banquan</term> <gloss>a legendary battlefield in North China</gloss>. He commanded bears, grizzly bears, wolves, leopards, <term>pixiu</term> <gloss>mythical fierce beasts</gloss>, and tigers as his vanguard. He used eagles, <term>he</term> <gloss>long-tailed pheasants</gloss>, falcons, and kites as his banners and standards. This is an example of using power to command birds and beasts. <term>Yao</term> <gloss>the sage king</gloss> appointed <term>Kui</term> <gloss>a legendary music master</gloss> to oversee music. When they struck and tapped the sounding stones, the hundred beasts led one another in dance. When the <term>Xiaoshao</term> <gloss>music of the sage king Shun</gloss> was performed nine times, the <term>fenghuang</term> <gloss>phoenixes</gloss> came to present themselves in ceremony. <note>This illustrates that sages can influence the natural world through both force and the harmony of music.</note>

<summary>This page discusses the disconnect between external physical appearance and internal moral character, citing ancient sages with animal features and tyrants with human features. It also describes how legendary kings like the Yellow Emperor and Yao commanded or harmonized with animals through power and music.</summary>
<keywords>Yellow Emperor, Flame Emperor, Banquan, virtue, appearance vs reality, Fuxi, Shennong, music, phoenix, legendary beasts</keywords>
